newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSIGHT - JGBs seen well-bid on investor demand.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - JGBs seen well-bid on investor demand.

text.p: Key June Japanese government bond (JGB) futures are likely to be well-supported in Thursday's Tokyo session on the back of investor demand for cash JGBs, traders said.

However, if bank stocks in Tokyo show a sharp rebound following news that Nippon Credit Bank and Bankers Trust New York Corp are in the "final stages" of talks on a business tie-up, JGBs' upside may become heavy, they said.
"The market will be watching how bank stocks react to the news of a tie-up," said a trader at a city bank's securities unit.

The recent heavy issuance of corporate straight bonds may also limit JGBs' upside potential in the near future, traders said. This week, over 300 billion yen worth of new straight bonds have been launched.
Market participants will be watching whether the Bank of Japan (BOJ) will conduct an outright bond purchase operation at 10.10 a.m. (0110 GMT).
"If the BOJ does not conduct outright bond buying this week, this could arouse speculation that the central bank may be considering reducing the amount of bond buying," said the trader.
A weaker yen may also weigh on JGBs, traders said.
The dollar ended at 126.85/90 yen in New York on Wednesday, after rising to a 56-month high of 127 yen.
Japan's machinery orders data for February will be released at 2 p.m. (0500 GMT) on Thursday.
"Machinery orders are unlikely to have a big impact on the market. A small decline is widely expected in February after a sharp rise in January," said a trader at another city bank's securities unit.
